correctness.rationale: For nonnegative nondecreasing data on \(P_n\), every fixed-radius centered ball average is nondecreasing as the center moves right: an interval either shifts right, gains a new largest value, loses an old smallest value, or is unchanged. The pointwise maximum over radii is therefore nondecreasing. At the left endpoint its maximal value is the global mean, while at the right endpoint it is the terminal value. Hence \(\operatorname{Var}(Mf)=f(n)-\overline f\). The elementary bound \(\overline f\ge((n-1)f(1)+f(n))/n\) gives the sharp factor \(1-1/n\), and equality for nonconstant data forces \(f(1)=\cdots=f(n-1)<f(n)\). Reflection gives the nonincreasing case. This proves the quantified theorem symbolically; finite checks are not needed for the infinite statement.
